Scope and evidence

This audit covers the FX2USD app at https://www.tocatlian.com/apps/fx/ in sc-domain:tocatlian.com, its URL variants, this source repository, and its GitHub Pages mirror. Other apps and root-host changes remain with their owning projects. Deployment and necessary GSC follow-up were authorized for justified fixes. Authorization does not establish an unverified production target.

Authenticated connector evidence was collected on November 17, 2026, beginning at approximately 17:54 UTC. Exact requests, responses, HTTP headers, live bodies, hashes, the PageSpeed receipt, and the minimal private Inbox ledger are retained locally in .cache/gsc-2026-11-17/. This ignored directory is excluded from generated documentation and the deployment allowlist. It contains no credentials or copied email bodies.

Search Analytics uses Web search, Pacific Time dates, final data, and this page filter: ^https?://(www\.)?tocatlian\.com/apps/fx(/|$). Each table request allowed 25,000 rows. At most one page row was returned, so no table reached its pagination limit. Empty query tables do not disclose anonymized queries or establish that no searches occurred.

The API freshness check identified November 16 as the first incomplete date. The recent supplement explicitly requested final data through November 15. Its raw zero-impression response encodes CTR and position as zero, which are not meaningful exposure metrics. The three-month figures are too sparse to support percentage growth, a ranking-loss diagnosis, seasonality adjustment, or a CTR experiment. The one returned landing page is the canonical URL.

Queries, query-by-page, devices, and countries returned no rows in the compared periods. Branded and nonbranded filters using the provisional expression (?i)(fx2usd|fx to usd|tocatlian) each returned zero disclosed impressions. They cannot reconcile the two aggregate impressions or establish the actual brand mix. There is no evidence for cannibalization or a high-impression, low-CTR query opportunity.

Gmail scope was received Search Console and Webmaster Tools notifications in the Inbox for FX2USD and its domain/path identifiers, without a date cutoff. Both scoped searches completed with no continuation token. Matching 0, reviewed 0, unresolved 0, moved to Trash 0, skipped 0, and cleanup failures 0. The coordinator separately reconciled domain-wide notifications. No other site's mail was acted on.

High

No issues at this severity were confirmed from the available evidence. The canonical landing page is indexed and accessible. The publishing gap found at baseline was operational, not a demonstrated deindexing event. The source-to-host relationship has now been established.

Medium

Canonical production publishing gap, recovered during this audit

  1. **The Issue:** Confirmed for FX2USD. This repository is the source owner, but .github/workflows/pages.yml deploys only https://tocatlian.github.io/fx2usd/. GitHub's Pages configuration reports that mirror URL, no custom domain, and workflow deployment. Baseline source commit b417bbe0e9f7e73696a94e7f74e5a563292df75c matched the mirror's HTML. At baseline, the canonical Apache URL returned different HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and manifest. Its HTML Last-Modified was July 30, 2026. The canonical and mirror HTML SHA-256 values are 116faaee74125437f594943a0cb4f363ece9308816b817a673d85636744982cd and bbbada89da4dcb4944b22d198e106b90387b9622cddbe69364f84dd161c11a0d, respectively. docs/local-maintenance.md already states that a HostGator command, connection configuration, and destination are missing. The root project reference explicitly leaves this app's publishing bridge unverified.
  2. **The Impact:** A successful Pages release cannot demonstrate that a correction reaches the indexed URL. The baseline production copy used external Google Fonts and predated current local accessibility, offline, and packaging improvements. This blocks a trustworthy canonical release and verification receipt. It does not establish a search ranking penalty or a current crawl-access failure.
  3. **The Code-Level Solution:** Recovered through the existing trusted shared-host connection without changing account access. At November 17, 2026, 18:07:56 UTC, read-only SFTP confirmed public_html/tocatlian.com/apps/fx. Its downloaded HTML and JavaScript hashes matched both canonical HTTPS responses exactly. Added scripts/deploy-hostgator.js, the private app-scoped .env.hostgator configuration, a credential-free example, and documented plan/apply commands. The uploader requires a clean committed checkout, the full quality gate, the fixed target and exact ten-file runtime allowlist. It backs up the remote app subtree, checks its HTML against live HTTPS before upload, uploads assets before HTML, and verifies every published file over SFTP and HTTPS. Its private receipt and rollback batch preserve predecessor evidence. Regression tests reject root, sibling and traversal destinations and command injection. README.md, PUBLISHING.md, and docs/local-maintenance.md now distinguish the canonical release from Pages and keep recurring deployment disabled. The authorized canonical release completed at 18:17:25.149 UTC with all ten runtime hashes matching over both SFTP and HTTPS. Its receipt is .cache/hostgator-releases/2026-11-17T18-17-09-513Z/receipt.json. The root sitemap lastmod update remains a root-project dependency after that release.

Shared-origin cache cleanup during the canonical upgrade

  1. **The Issue:** Confirmed in sw.js while preparing the first canonical release of the current PWA. Activation deleted every cache other than the current FX2USD cache. The canonical host also serves sibling applications. The baseline canonical app had no service worker, so this was a prospective deployment regression rather than an observed indexing failure.
  2. **The Impact:** Activating this release could discard sibling apps' cached files. This affects offline behavior and user experience, not direct indexability. Releasing the existing worker unchanged would violate the campaign's requirement to preserve other projects.
  3. **The Code-Level Solution:** Restricted cleanup to names beginning with fx2usd-app-v, retaining unrelated caches. Updated tests/sw.test.js to keep a seeded sibling-app cache through installation and activation while removing the stale FX cache. The package and worker version are both 0.1.1. The full quality gate passes with 22 tests. Deployment verification includes the worker file hash. No root or sibling cache code was changed.

Low

Limited explanatory content for the converter

  1. **The Issue:** Confirmed source observation for FX2USD, with unmeasured search impact. At baseline, both index.html and the canonical HTML mainly exposed controls, results, banknotes, and history. They lacked a short visible explanation of rate direction, manual overrides, cached rates, and practical limitations. This bounded content gap is now corrected in the deployed release. Current disclosed search volume is insufficient to identify a specific missing query or substantiate a CTR opportunity.
  2. **The Impact:** Concise instructions could help new visitors understand the app and give search systems useful visible context. No traffic gain or AI citation is established. Existing discovery is present through the root sitemap and the root site's coding-journey page, so the app is not a confirmed orphan.
  3. **The Code-Level Solution:** Added a visible usage section in index.html after the app's history section. It explains currency selection, the USD result, live and saved rates, manual USD-per-unit quotes, banknotes, and on-device history using behavior verified in app.js. No duplicate currency pages or speculative rating schema were added. The full quality gate passes. Post-release HTTPS confirms that the final section is present in the indexable document. Chrome rendering and live/manual conversion checks remain pending the shared browser lease. Measure query-by-page exposure over complete later periods before attributing any movement to this text.

Root sitemap modification date after the verified release

  1. **The Issue:** Confirmed cross-project dependency for FX2USD. At 18:25:57 UTC after the verified release, the root sitemap still listed https://www.tocatlian.com/apps/fx/ with lastmod of July 30, 2026. The app is present and indexed, so this is stale discovery metadata rather than a missing sitemap entry.
  2. **The Impact:** The sitemap does not describe this substantive November 17 update accurately. Correcting the date gives Google a truthful discovery signal, without guaranteeing a recrawl or ranking change.
  3. **The Code-Level Solution:** The root site's owning project should update only the FX entry in its sitemap.xml to <lastmod>2026-11-17</lastmod>, use its documented build and deployment procedure, and verify the live XML. The root owner controls any subsequent root-sitemap resubmission. This app project does not edit or deploy the sibling repository. The verified canonical release receipt and source commit above provide the prerequisite evidence.

Release and remaining work

The canonical publishing gap was recovered rather than left as an unresolved ownership assumption. The production directory was verified through authenticated SFTP and exact live hashes at 18:07:56 UTC. Initial subsequent transfers closed or reset before authentication, then a later read-only full backup succeeded. The release used the same trusted SSH connection and did not change account access or host trust.

PR #31 merged after successful Node.js 22 and 24 CI. Canonical release commit 2130bb1636645a55e2df1b966af1a469642f4180 is tagged v0.1.1. Its deployment began November 17, 2026 at 18:17:09.513 UTC and completed verification at **18:17:25.149 UTC**, or **10:17:25 a.m. Pacific**. All ten runtime files matched the package through independent SFTP downloads and HTTPS requests. The receipt, complete predecessor snapshot, rollback batch, and verification bodies are under .cache/hostgator-releases/2026-11-17T18-17-09-513Z/. The new canonical HTML SHA-256 is d3039d98a770e9288cd6b84a8a195b0bf4b13fe322d42d3a5d488e3695ec88a3.

The automatic Pages mirror run 44146103751 also succeeded for the same source commit. It is a separate deployment receipt and was not used as evidence of canonical publishing.

Post-release HTTP checks at 18:18:21 UTC confirmed 200 delivery, one correct canonical, indexable robots signals, the new instructions, no Google Fonts request in HTML, direct 301 normalization of apex and trailing-slash variants, and a real 404 for a missing child page. The service worker and PWA screenshot now return the exact package bytes as part of the ten-file verification. Those two paths were intentionally absent in the older live version, which did not reference them.

The post-release mobile PageSpeed sample at 18:18:23.846 UTC scored 98, with LCP 1207.90 ms, TBT 0 ms, CLS 0, and Speed Index 3760.46 ms. It returned no field data or listed opportunities. The earlier sample scored 99. These are single lab samples, not proof of a performance trend or a field Core Web Vitals pass.

Google's post-release indexed-version check remains **pending recrawl**. The page is indexed, its canonical matches, and its last reported crawl is still August 17, 2026 at 02:58:18 UTC. Deployment is verified independently of Google's eventual crawl, indexing refresh, field data, and search performance changes.

The original local main has a pre-existing divergent history commit and was preserved. Deployment ran from a clean release branch based on merged origin/main, without resetting or rebasing the user's local history. Private configuration, audit evidence, and backups are ignored and excluded from both deployment packages.

Shared property Chrome evidence

The Newsroom project collected rendered accessibility snapshots in the existing signed-in Chrome browser for the same sc-domain:tocatlian.com property on November 17, 2026, from 18:35 through 18:40 UTC. Its curated observation record and transcript provenance are referenced by the minimal copied context file in this project's private evidence directory. This is reused first-party UI evidence, not a claim that this FX task independently visited those reports.

Manual actions and Security issues both showed **No issues detected**. Core Web Vitals, updated November 8, showed **Not enough usage data in the last 90 days** separately for mobile and desktop. This is insufficient data, not a field pass or failure.

The observed Breadcrumbs, Image Metadata, and Profile Page enhancement reports, updated November 15, showed zero invalid items. FX implements none of those markup types, and the property-level valid counts are not an FX inventory. The HTTPS report, updated November 16, showed no issues detected in the last 90 days. FX's actual HTTPS delivery is independently verified in this project. Other projects' Performance, sitemap, indexing counts, article findings, and URL examples were not copied into the FX findings.
